chunks: Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ziyād ibn Abī Rajāʾ, from Abū Hāshim al-Jawfī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Imām al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever starts his day with the world as his greatest concern, Allah will scatter his affair, and his poverty will be in front of his eyes, and nothing of this world will come to him except that which has been destined for him. And whoever’s greatest concern is the Hereafter, Allah will remove his constraints for him, gather his affair, and this world will come to him in submission.

key_terms.فَقْرُهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ: His poverty was in front of his eyes (visible lack)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between focusing on the world versus the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* encapsulates the Shia concept of *Tawakkul* by contrasting the psychological and spiritual fragmentation caused by making the world the ultimate goal with the divine ease (*Faraaj*) granted to those who prioritize the Hereafter. It reflects the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt that true wealth is not material accumulation but the sufficiency of God's decree, where the world becomes a willing servant to the believer rather than a master.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 12.Faḍālah narrates from Abān, from Ziyād ibn Abī Rajāʾ, from Abū Hishām, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “

Whoever starts his day with the world as his greatest concern [and objective], Allah will scatter his affair and his poverty will be [seen] in front of him, and nothing of this world will come to him except that which has been destined for him. But whoever’s greatest concern is the Hereafter, Allah will remove his constraints for him and gather his affair, and this world will come to him in [complete] submission.”
